newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent MD sees action soon on UK newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Independent MD sees action soon on UK newspapers.

text.p: The Irish government appears to be moving toward action on the issue of below-cost selling by British newspapers in the Irish market, David Palmer, managing director of Independent Newspapers Plc said.
Speaking to the Leinster Society of Chartered Accountants on Friday, Palmer said this would be very much welcomed by the Irish newspaper industry.
"The whole industry welcomes the Irish government's commitment to finding a way of ending the below-cost attack on the indigenous industry," he said.

He noted that the first newspaper commission in the history of the Irish state concluded last year that an indigenous newspaper industry was fundamental to the well being of Irish society and democracy.
Palmer also said the Irish newspaper industry needed to improve its competitiveness against British imports.
"Independent Newspapers has estimated that the production labour cost per page for producing a newspaper in Ireland is over four times the equivalent in Fleet Street."
Palmer also called on the government to abolish value-added-tax on newspapers in Ireland so create a more level playing field.
He also said it was too easy for libel actions to be launched in Ireland and both the damages awarded and the cost of defending them had become prohibitive.
Independent Newspapers is Ireland's largest newspaper group.
